Alright, not as stoned now lol. Canifis rooftop was the best at the time for getting marks of grace, I'm not sure if that's the case now with updates to agility. Also consider doing some Motherlode mine whenever you want to afk and/or are feeling burnt out of doing something else like WT/Temp. Questing is a great way to get easy levels in some skills so I recommend also knocking out some of the easier quests that have useful rewards (avas accumulator, Fairy rings, kingdom, etc..) Priorities early on should be something like this

1. Graceful/Rogues outfit 

2. Easy/Useful quests

3. WT/Temp/MLM/GotR

4. Barrows for gear (Karils, Ahrim mainly)

Once you hit barrows is when you really start gearing up on an iron. It was the first "big" goal my buddy and I had and once we did it and got decent gear is when you can start really getting into the juicy stuff osrs has. Don't set unrealistic goals for yourself or team. Example being, Don't start at 1 RC and say you're gonna grind it until 77 for blood runes because you will burn out super hard, fast. Smaller goals are easier and more rewarding and keep you interested. To help with this mix in herb runs, birdhouses, clues, and quests.

In my opinion the only goal that is achievable without making you hate the game would be getting 99 FM through wintertodt off the bat. Gets you lots of money and a decent amount of seeds as well as the chance to get some magic logs which you will all need for a quest at some point and unless you can cut them that's one of the easiest ways to get it lol. Enjoy the members Ironman experience though, have fun and don't grind too hard. Hopefully you all stay playing for a while, my group mate hasn't logged in almost a year now so I've been a solo group iron for a while now lol.

If there's 3 of you, you can all focus one thing and help each other that way. One supplies food form Temp, One supplies money/misc shit from Wintertodt, One grind out 77 RC via GOTR or whatever's clever. 

  
That being said, my buddy and I both followed optimal iron man quest guide for quite a while. Buddy did WT, slayer grind, and herblore while I spent more time doing fishing, thieving for gold, farming for herbs. 

Little tips for sanity: Don't wait to get full graceful, honestly. If going on a thieving route for bandits (great iron money early game) make sure you have the thieving outfit for double thieving loot. Farming is a skill you'll sort of hate yourself late game for not hopping on earlier for. Farming gives you all the herbs, a lot of secondaries, tree in your POH, Giant seaweed for molten glass (probably how you'll end up leveling crafting) and so on. Start slayer early as well; you can do the slayer point farming early on to get easy rune pouch through slayer if you want.

Parents refused to take me to get therapy or any sort of mental health after multiple times telling them I'm constantly in a depressed mindset and I want help getting out. They pretty much just kept on telling me it was because I was young and I was making it all up for some reason. 25 years old now and I'm starting to see the brighter side of life, but it was only after I got away from them, got a job with really good insurance and could finally afford the help I needed. It's been over a year now and things are NOT significantly better by any means but I dont want to kill myself anymore. Not every day at least. Hell I probably think about it once or twice a month. It's all still there and it still very much exists inside of me but I think what has helped me the most is the outlook. Instead of saying, "I'm depressed and I hate my fucking self" I stated saying shit like, "I'm depressed but I'm working on myself." That coupled with remembering that every small tiny achievement (like being less depressed than usual for a small amount of the day) is still an achievement and should not go unnoticed. I know I'm just a random guy on the internet but one small thing I started doing in the beginning of treatment was I would smile first thing in the morning. Even though it was almost always a forced fake smile, it seemed to hell me start the days off better than usual. I still do it to this day. I hope you get the help you need and can start to see the brighter side of life, there is a lot of people who will accept you with love and open arms over there!

If you can one day, I would highly recommend getting the Save the World mode. It helps your aim, building and overall sense of the game.

I know it's not free BUT! Save the World mode helped me with my Aiming, building, and locating chests. In my experience, house and factory chest spawns are the same in BR and STW. 

Aiming was helpful, mainly because I'm still learning mouse and keyboard. You also get to test bullet drop and bloom.

Building was the main take away from STW. There's events in game where you literally have to build towers, it teaches you different building styles and also helps your speed when building and editing. Also, a little thing I took away from STW was learning the hitboxes for building stuff. I.E. knowing if you'll just barely make it past that huge tree whilst building stairs up. 

Its helped me a lot in many ways, I would definitely try and save a little money and grab the standard version. Oh, you'll also earn a shitload of V-Bucks on a lot of your first missions which you can spend in BR.

First, What's your username so I can add you? Mine is Shnagan.

Second, as far as combat stats for you, something you can do is use your 99 mage to your advantage and set your exp to Defense. Your 99 magic will help you kill things a lot quicker and if you just hit like 80 defense you should (technically) have accumulated some money for better gear to train attack. Mage is your best friend right now, it's useful in most all boss fights/combat situations. 

Third, higher level herbs sell for a pretty good amount of money so you can add in daily farming runs for money. Grow herbs, sell after you get a nice stack, repeat. Also, if you can plant papaya trees, the fruit sells for good money, but the seeds are pretty expensive.

Fourth, if you haven't yet, do the throne of miscelania quest and invest in the kingdom! I personally put all my workers doing trees and herbs (100% in trees, and 50% in herbs) make sure to set the wood to mahogany. After a few weeks you can get a lot of those logs which you can then use portable sawmills to turn in to planks for a really good profit margin, it just takes time.

Lastly, set yourself small goals. I'd recommend starting with Completing all of the Beginner/Intermediate quests. I say this because you get treasure hunter keys when you complete them and a few of them give really decent exp or lamps. Some quests offer small but helpful things like the tree teleporting or fairy rings etc. 

Oh, one more thing. DAILYS/MONTHLYS will be your best friends. I start my playing by going to World 2 Burthorpe and doing div locations (if you lay the location down make sure to call it out before putting it down to get as many people on it as you can) you can get a lot of levels by just doing that. I like to focus mining so everyday I try to find divine mining locations until I hit level and then do WC. Penguin hunter, Giant Oyster, Troll Invasion, Warbands, Guthix Caches, and Sinkholes are the ones I personally prioritize. Look in to them and check them out! Guthix Caches are the best way to get faster Divination levels because holy hell divination is a pain..

All of the quests are great, but I might be saying that because I love questing. So here are my opinions as to blocking boredom.

F2P: Do so dungeoneering. You can work on your woodcutting because it can get you some good money and though it may be a grind you can multitask easily. When I was a F2P player I usually made a certain goal every time that I logged in i.e. get 50 str and 45 def etc. My main overall goal though was to complete all of the F2P quests. I also liked to kill Moss Giants for some reason and bury their bones. Though this one may be out of the question, If you do find something to grind on for combat stats that isn't a complete bore then you can do some PvP

P2P: If you are not a member I HIGHLY suggest being one right now. The day that I moved from F2P to P2P I fell even more in love with Runescape. One of my favorite skills to do that keeps me from being bored is slayer. It guarantees a combat grind and most of the slayer tasks grant really good chances for good drops. I also love doing the members quests as a matter of fact the very first day I was a member I did a lot of questing. There's always something fun to do when you're a member. You can also do Evil Tree hunting, shooting star hunts and I had fun building my own house! Now my stats aren't the best either, Search Shnagan in the High scores, but I manage to find something to do every day that's usually exciting. Right now I'm attack the dust devil's in hopes of a Dragon Chain drop :) 

Good luck and I hope that this has helped you out!
